sources.text: 1.2.4 Define the chemical name, generic name, and trade name of drugs. 1.2.5 Explain the difference between a drug’s generic and brand name equivalents. 1.2.6 Differentiate between prescription and over-the-counter drugs. 1.2.7 Compare and contrast traditional drugs, biologics, and alternative and complementary drug therapies. Drug Sources and Forms Drugs are substances or compounds that prevent, treat, diagnose, or cure various conditions or diseases. As mentioned previously, drugs come from a variety of resources—plants, animal products, and inorganic substances. Ideally, these chemicals have desirable therapeutic effects without harmful properties, although many derivatives may have poisonous effects, depending upon the dosage used. sources.text: 6.4 Introduction to the Inflammatory Response and Anti-inflammatory Drugs Learning Outcomes By the end of this section, you should be able to: 6.4.1 Describe the pathophysiology of inflammation. 6.4.2 Discuss the five cardinal signs of inflammation. 6.4.4 Identify the characteristics of drugs used to treat inflammation. 6.4.5 Explain the indications, actions, adverse reactions, and interactions of drugs used to treat inflammation. 6.4.6 Describe the nursing implications of drugs used to treat inflammation. 6.4.7 Explain the client education related to drugs used to treat inflammation. Inflammation, the body’s complex response to harmful stimuli, plays an important role in the immune system’s defense against injury and infection.
